description: A gate sequencer that plays Morse code: each clock pulse is one Morse time unit, dots run for one unit and dashes for three, and the gate output rises and falls through the pattern

inputs.text: One Morse time unit per rising edge above 1V; the module produces nothing at all until a cable is patched here

outputs.text: A 0 to 10V gate, high through a dot or a dash and low through the gaps

notes: This module was shipped unfinished. The characters it plays are picked at random rather than read from any file, so what comes out is a Morse-shaped gate pattern rather than readable Morse.
The table that turns a character into dots and dashes was filled in wrongly, so every letter plays the code for A, every digit the code for zero and every punctuation the code for ampersand.
Four more inputs and one knob are configured in the module and drawn nowhere on the panel, their widgets commented out as work in progress. No cable and no click can reach them.
The lamp near the bottom of the panel is drawn but never lit: nothing in the module writes it.
With no cable at the clock input the module returns before it sets the output, so the output jack keeps whatever voltage it last had.
menu: Data File — opens a file chooser and stores the path you pick, but nothing in the module ever reads that file: the characters played are drawn at random instead

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
